title: Grok trade
body:
Me: What is an attractive call option  with catalyst and some fundamentals? Use expiration dates between 12/15/2025 and 6/4/2026. Current price of stock preferably under $40. Premiums under $3. Looking for something that could run fast.

Grok: One attractive call option fitting your criteria is the Ford Motor Company (F) December 19, 2025 $14 call. The stock’s current price is around $12.43 (well under $40), and this option’s premium (last price) is $0.17, with a bid/ask of $0.17/$0.20. It’s slightly out-of-the-money, offering leverage for quick upside if the stock moves.
Catalyst: Ford reports Q3 earnings tomorrow (October 23, 2025), with analysts expecting EPS of $0.35 and revenue of $47 billion. Positive results, especially on EV sales or cost controls amid industry shifts, could drive a rapid price surge—Ford has seen 5-10% single-day moves post-earnings in the past.
Fundamentals: Ford is a legacy automaker with a market cap over $50 billion, strong cash flow from its truck lineup (e.g., F-150), and growth in EVs like the Mustang Mach-E. It pays a ~5% dividend yield, has a forward P/E around 7, and is undervalued relative to peers amid auto sector recovery. Debt is manageable, and management is focusing on profitability in electric vehicles.
This setup has potential for a fast run if earnings beat, given the short time to expiration (about 2 months) and low premium for high return on capital if the stock hits $14.50+ breakeven quickly. Options data sourced from Yahoo Finance.

title: Home Owners Insurance
body:
I have owned a franchise of the largest restoration company in the US for 15 years. I have dealt with pretty much every insurance company and their adjusters that does business in AR/TN/MS. Ten years ago I would have loved it if every job was a State Farm job. These days they may be the worst insurance company in America if you ever need to file a claim. Absolutely fucking terrible. And honestly, most of them have gotten much worse over the past 5-10 years. But State Farm has fallen way further than anyone else. My employees got no Christmas bonuses this year. I had to use credit card points for my kids Christmas. All because State Farm owes me a lot of money for work that has been complete 45-90 days. Most homeowners have trouble even paying their deductible much less our whole bill. So 95% of my customers can not pay me until their insurance company pays them. 

I am very proficient in dealing with claims and adjusters. Don’t ever just accept an adjuster denying your claim unless you knew it was questionable from the beginning. I’ve helped several customers over the years get claims covered that were initially denied. Most denials are justified, but not all. And State Farm has adopted a deny first policy. Also, don’t ever let your adjuster guide your choices, tell you who you need to use, or tell you your contractor is over charging. 90% of us use the same program with a dedicated price list that the insurance companies use. When you have a claim, who’s your ally, the person that wants to pay you as little as possible or the person that wants you to have your home back with as little cost to you as possible? 

I say all this for this reason, if you have a claim and you feel like you aren’t being treated unfairly by your insurance company, I will be happy to take a look at your situation for you and give guidance. I do charge a small consulting fee, but not unless I am able to help you get more money or get your claim covered. But I will look at it for free. Unless y’all flood me with requests that pull me away from my paying business. Then I may have to charge a little for my time.

title: Dead
body:
Somewhere around the mid to late 80’s the Grateful Dead made a video for MTV for the song Touch of Grey (I believe the only one they did). I was early teens and had heard of them, but just associated them with hippies and Woodstock. But being the quintessential MTV generation, now I was hearing them. Several years later I really started going down the rabbit hole. I was living in Nebraska in 1995 and was moving back to Tennessee in a few months. They were playing the pyramid in Memphis in April and I was moving back in June so I didn’t go home to see my first show. But I was happy that they were playing my hometown and thought I’d catch them next year. There was no next year. Never saw Jerry. 

You can go deep into the members of the GD. But for me, there were three that really drew me in. Jerry of course. Phil, especially with The Other Ones. And Bobby. Got to see Bob a few times with Ratdog. Never went to a dead & co show. But today, with Bobby’s passing, and with Phil’s passing a little while back, there is no form of the Grateful Dead left. Anything from this point forward is a cover band. And I’ll go. God speed Bobby.

title: Ortho/PT
body:
Any ortho or physical therapy people in here. I tore my distal bicep tendon about a year and a half ago. The repair failed. My terrible doctor would not listen to me and insisted it was fine. Told me to give it a few months. In those months I stewed about him totally dismissing me so I researched a bit and went to another doc in another city who specializes in elbow/shoulder. As I suspected, the repair had failed. And this is an injury with a time window that had now passed. I’ve had some discomfort in the other one when lifting palm up so I am really hindered on carrying anything over about 10 lbs palm up. What I am trying to figure out is how to get back in the gym and rebuild strength without injuring myself. The fear of tearing the other one just keeps me out of the gym. And I despise any running or highly aerobic excercise. Two ankle surgeries and questionable knees. At 51 now (still 30 in my mind) my ass just can’t readjust to a road bike seat, which I really enjoyed in my 20’s. So I’d rather just stick with weight or resistance training. Any advice on shoulder/arm/chest rehab and strengthening would be much appreciated. No regular curls. No bench press. I can do most everything in my day to day with that left arm, but it’s like the elbow geometry is just all wrong now. I wouldn’t trust it on bench and the curl motion with palm up is what causes this injury. Help a beat up and battered old man out.  Baseball, football and car wrecks have wreaked havoc on my joints. 

PS - my kid is the only person who doesn’t get at least a little nervous in the car with me. 

PPS - the two wrecks that really got me hurt, I was drunk. Like 2.0+ bac. I had a minor accident when my family was out of town after a night with the boys when my kid was about 5. Also close to the time UBER starting coming along. Last time I drove in that condition. UBER probably saved my life. Or at least heartache, headaches and money. 

PPPS - California sober now. And from the rambling post, right now.
